biography.plain_text: François Fontès is a French architect and property developer from Montpellier. He established his architectural practice in 1975 and later built Hugar, a group spanning design, engineering and development. His businesses include Amétis, which he co-founded to develop social and intermediate housing, and his projects range from schools to urban neighbourhoods.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Montpellier’s medical faculty, architect François Fontès used slender columns and a perforated roof to bring shifting patterns of light into the entrance spaces. His interest in local materials also shaped other projects: stone from Pompignan supplied paving for the Jean Monnet lycée, while timber from Le Vigan clad social housing at Palavas.

He also helped return L’Architecture d’Aujourd’hui to print. At Jean Nouvel’s prompting, Fontès and businessman Alexandre Allard bought the magazine and created Archipress & Associés to publish it. After nearly two years without an issue, the journal resumed its bimonthly schedule in November 2009.
